questions.question: A company buys new servers for its on-premises datacenter. What type of expenditure is this?

options.why: Correct. Up-front purchase of physical assets.
OpEx is ongoing spending on services as you use them.
This is not a real expenditure category.

questions.explanation: Purchasing physical infrastructure up front is CapEx.

questions.question: Paying a monthly bill for Azure virtual machines based on usage is an example of what?

options.why: No asset is purchased up front.
Correct. Ongoing spending for services consumed.
The bill is ongoing and usage-based.

questions.explanation: Cloud consumption is billed as operational expenditure.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about operational expenditure (OpEx) are true?

options.text: It requires a large up-front investment
Costs can be adjusted as needs change
options.why: Correct. You can scale usage up or down.

options.text: It is spent on services or products as they are used
The asset is owned and depreciated over years

questions.explanation: OpEx is ongoing, usage-based and flexible; CapEx is up-front and depreciated.

questions.scenario: A company wants to avoid a large initial investment and only pay for IT resources as the business grows.
questions.question: Which approach meets this goal?

options.why: That is a large CapEx investment.

options.text: Use cloud services billed through a consumption-based model
options.why: Correct. OpEx with no up-front cost.

options.text: Buy servers with a five-year warranty

questions.explanation: Cloud consumption-based pricing avoids up-front investment and scales with the business.
